Read the bounded, customer-scoped Numbers aggregate
get.description: Returns the read-only data needed by the Numbers dashboard, including workspace-wide number_allowance (used, limit, remaining, can_add; null limit means no billed-number cap). Each number includes calling_readiness: bounded inbound routing/pricing blockers and destination-dependent outbound configuration. Outbound registration_status distinguishes pending, failed, registered, not_required and legacy; pending or failed caller-ID registration blocks outbound only and is retried independently of carrier-ready inbound activation. DIDWW capacity pricing can report capacity_hybrid_unsupported, capacity_separate_metering_unsupported, or capacity_plan_unavailable; these refuse only the affected number. Inbound readiness remains indeterminate when mandatory call-time admission checks were not evaluated; a purchased number is not proof that calls can connect. The aggregate is tenant-bound to the bearer session, makes no provider calls or writes, and excludes provider internals, secrets, billing history, calls, SMS, and verification documents. Pass project_id for an explicit project; when omitted, the response returns its selected default project. Bounded collections expose truncation flags rather than silently implying a complete export.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Calls aggregate
get.description: Public customer API for the Calls workspace view: the newest page of call history with its real total, the selected call's observability detail, the workspace agents, the latest trial, and the compact wallet snapshot the shared workspace header uses. It also reports, per call, which workflow version ran and a compact path through it -- step ids, chosen routes, tool statuses and sanitized policy reasons -- plus the full turn-grouped trace for the selected call. A selected transcript turn's has_audio flag is true only while an active recording and its linked turn clip are available; clients use the authenticated recording relay rather than a storage or artifact identifier. A call that ran no workflow is ABSENT from workflow_evidence rather than present and empty. Bound to the bearer session organization; it never accepts an arbitrary organization, calls a provider, reconciles state, or writes data. The call's internal runtime configuration is never returned, and neither is a run's pinned contract. Both the path per row and the trace are bounded and report truncation; detail=0 omits the selected call's observability and its trace for routine freshness polls.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Calls Performance aggregate
get.description: Public customer API for the Calls Performance workspace view. It is bound to the bearer session organization; it never accepts an arbitrary organization, calls a provider, parses object storage, reconciles state, or writes data. It includes the compact wallet snapshot used by the shared workspace header, but no billing history. Pass call_id only for a call in the selected project. Existing calls without a normalized call-telemetry artifact return evidence.status=unavailable and no fabricated spans. The bounded spans collection is ordered by turn, offset, stage, and attempt; audit correlation IDs, raw prompts, queries, passages, and secrets are never returned.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Overview aggregate
get.description: Returns one read-only workspace DTO for Overview SSR and freshness polling. Call rows include the compact component_billing wallet verdict used by Calls, without billing line items. Each number carries incoming_rule -- what that line does when it is called -- resolved for every number in one batched read, so the page can say which lines answer without a request per number. knowledge reports how many active knowledge bases the workspace has and how many documents are in them, as two counts rather than the bases themselves. The aggregate is tenant-bound to the bearer session, uses no provider calls, and omits provider internals, full verification profiles, secrets, invoices, and voice-stack configuration.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped Agents aggregate
get.description: Returns one tenant-bound Agents DTO for SSR. It includes resolved static voice-stack display data, which components the customer actually configured (as opposed to the catalog defaults the resolved stack fills in), an inbound-admission verdict per agent, attached number routing, exact UTC-day activity, each agent's measured reply time (the median of its recorded worker-side reply turns, or an explicit unavailable when nothing was measured -- never a component-constant estimate presented as an observation), and wallet currency without provider or catalog API calls, verification, invoice, SMS, or webhook service reads. The admission verdict is a pure read of workspace state: `admits`/`readiness` reflect only conditions the inbound call path itself would refuse over; `blockers` is not a strict subset of those -- a small, explicitly declared set of codes (currently a misconfigured transfer_to_human destination) is real and actionable but does not affect `admits`/`readiness`, because invoking that tool mid-call fails gracefully rather than refusing the call. `unevaluated` lists the conditions the read could not evaluate before a call exists, and `readiness` is blocked or indeterminate — never ready, because the gates that need the agent's number are not run here. A line-scoped readiness is reported by the Overview aggregate's primary_line. An agent answered by the customer's own service is judged on the endpoints it needs rather than on the managed stack it does not use.

get.summary: Read the bounded, customer-scoped hosted-agent editor aggregate
get.description: Returns one selected agent, its resolved stack including saved turn_taking, voice_polish and audio_environment settings, which components were actually configured, the same inbound-admission verdict the Agents list carries, the launch-supported component-metered catalog, a wallet projection, a bounded metadata-only BYOK credential list, and the agent's measured reply time: the median of a bounded sample of its recorded worker-side reply turns, reported as unavailable rather than zero until real calls exist. That figure ends when the first audio frame leaves the worker, so carrier transit and remote playout are not in it. It is bound to the dashboard session organization and selected project; it never decrypts credentials, calls a provider, validates a key, or writes state.

get.summary: Read the workspace's capabilities record, the selectable use-case profiles, and live usage against its caps
get.description: Pure read. Every workspace has exactly one record from creation on: `capabilities.status` is `not_activated` until the workspace clears verification (an operator's business review, or its first registration-free number), when it becomes `active` on the default profile, the channels the workspace holds and every destination except the sanctioned set (`all_countries: true`). `pending_review` means a request is with an Skysay operator and nothing new is authorized yet; `suspended` means an operator paused outbound. When `all_countries` is false, `countries` is the explicit allowlist (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). `calling_rules` is the application cadence contract an operator recorded on approval, or null, and `calling_rules_active` says whether it is enforced right now. Every outbound call and SMS is authorized against this record (see POST /v1/policies/authorize-outbound).

post.summary: Request or change the workspace's capabilities
post.description: Select the use-case profiles, channels and destinations outbound should be authorized for, and accept the outbound policy by sending `policy_version`. The destination choice is explicit: `all_countries: true` (every destination except the sanctioned set) or `countries` naming at least one well-formed ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A request with neither, with an empty list, or with an entry that is not a two-letter code is refused with 400 and nothing is written, so an active allowlist is never widened or emptied by a request that was refused. A verified workspace that accepts the policy and selects no custom profile is activated immediately within the profiles' default caps; anything else opens an Skysay review, and what is already active stays active until the review resolves. `calling_rules` cannot be set here; an operator records them on approval.

get.summary: List runnable agent stack entries
get.description: Pass metered_only=true to receive only the launch-supported hosted components with a runtime adapter, native meter, pinned retail rate, and safe credential contract (validated BYOK where supported or an explicit platform-managed provider contract). The payload also includes conversation_engines: cascade (default STT/LLM/TTS) and gpt_live (GPT-Live-1 voices and Responses backends). A TTS row uses either immutable worker-approved voices or bounded provider-directory voices already ingested by Skysay; the catalog never fetches a provider during a read. Voice metadata and tags are provider-supplied and carry provenance; Skysay does not infer age, accent, or personality. When a provider supplies no per-voice language list, the row inherits only its qualified TTS model languages. voice_count and voices_truncated say when a provider inventory is partial. A resolved agent preserves its exact selected voice in its voice-stack response even outside a bounded catalog slice. Every TTS row carries `delivery_control`: `voice_settings`, `instruction` or `speed` when a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes that engine's audio, or `unsupported` when the engine accepts and stores a profile without changing its audio (Fish Audio and Azure neural voices today); and `delivery_profiles`, the exact value each of the four profiles resolves to on that engine (a settings object such as stability/similarity_boost/style/speed, a speaking rate, or an instruction sentence), empty for `unsupported`. Both are read from the same packaged delivery table the call runtime and the voice preview use, so a client can state what a profile changes for a voice without a provider list of its own. This catalog does not authorize a provider credential or disclose provider secrets.

The route derives the organization exclusively from the bearer principal and rejects organization_id rather than accepting an arbitrary tenant selector. It returns only organization id/name and project id/name/environment in stable created_at,id order, with an exact count and explicit page metadata. It works for an empty-agent starter workspace and never reads users, credentials, provider/operator data, or secrets; it makes no provider call and performs no write, repair, or lazy creation.

post.summary: Render one bounded managed voice-selector preview
post.description: An explicit Listen action for one selected TTS voice. It accepts a bounded caller sentence (defaulting to a short product sample only when no audio_environment is supplied), keeps no audio or telemetry, and returns a short in-memory WAV only. A selected outgoing audio_environment requires explicit non-blank text and makes a deterministic, headroom-safe local audition; it never substitutes the text, language, voice, or claims a receiver-side final mix. A small per-workspace fixed-window limit protects provider spend. Every language a provider advertises can be previewed. On a platform credential the voice must be one the workspace could browse and select, except an existing saved hosted agent may re-test its exact current platform-managed selection by supplying agent_id when it has disappeared from a listing; arbitrary typed IDs never create shared runtime evidence. With a selected BYOK credential the credential is validated at the provider and then used to render, so any voice id that provider accepts works, and a platform credential is never a fallback. A GPT-Live-1 voice (provider openai, model gpt-live-1) previews differently: it is a short real live session on the platform credential that speaks Skysay's own sample sentence for the requested language, rendered once per voice, language and sample and then served from a tenant-agnostic cache (the response carries text_source: platform_sample and cached). Typed text is refused with error code voice_preview_fixed_sample rather than replaced, credential_id and delivery do not apply, a platform-wide concurrency cap answers 429 when every preview slot is busy, and the preview is never metered as a call.

400.description: Invalid tenant-bound project, stack, voice, preview text, audio_environment, or a BYOK credential the provider did not accept; also typed text for a GPT-Live-1 voice (voice_preview_fixed_sample)

404.description: The selected BYOK credential does not exist in this workspace

409.description: The selected voice cannot be previewed in the requested language

429.description: Voice-preview fixed-window limit reached, or every platform-wide GPT-Live preview slot is busy

get.summary: List immutable audio-environment presets

The catalogue is a pure local read: it contacts no TTS provider, makes no carrier call, changes no agent setting and returns no audio bytes. `off` is explicit. An agent's outgoing selection always pins preset id, asset version and volume; Simulation Lab's separate caller-input condition pins the same id/version with noise_level. Callers must not invent a frontend catalogue, silently substitute a retired version, or pass output ambience to STT.

patch.summary: Validate and update a hosted agent's STT, model, and TTS selections
patch.description: The target agent defines the authenticated workspace. Select platform-managed components by provider/model/voice fields, or bind a component to an already-created hosted-AI credential by its ID in component_credential_bindings. The binding is a reference only: upload a BYOK secret through the separate write-only hosted-ai-credentials API; this route never accepts or returns secret material. Supplying languages and optional sparse language_profiles is an explicit publication: all effective profiles are constructible and credential-owned before an immutable version is stored for admission. `audio_environment` is a separately version-pinned outgoing-only ambience track, shared across language profiles and independent of caller STT; its optional runtime failure never replaces the selected voice/language or prevents the core call. Draft profile edits never alter existing calls or published sessions.

post.summary: Create an authenticated LiveKit browser-test session for one hosted agent
post.description: Workspace-authenticated only. Does not use the anonymous homepage demo budget. New sessions reserve eligible browser-only welcome credit or purchased funds and settle actual component usage; no carrier charge applies. The existing session limit is 180 seconds. Historical zero-charge snapshots remain unchanged. The selected snapshot is published or a validated draft overlay. A draft overlay naming an unknown, retired, or language-incompatible selection is rejected with a plain 400 before this point, as before. A silence turn needs the adaptive_voice runner and is refused with 422 silence_needs_a_room on any other, because only a room has time to spend. An adaptive_voice scenario may also carry caller_environment: a version-pinned synthetic caller MICROPHONE condition using noise_level (not the agent audio_environment volume). A scenario that supplies caller_environment must use adaptive_voice and also supply a non-blank language; it is never silently changed to English. Off/noise_level=0 is the quiet baseline; it never changes the agent's output ambience, TTS, or production STT configuration. A saved condition is authoring data, not proof that this deployment ran a realtime room.

This is a pure, provider-free reconciliation read: it does not create calls, retry recipients, classify a business outcome, or copy recordings/transcripts. It returns authoritative technical call facts and a versioned, allowlisted technical_failure envelope separately from optional advisory extraction, plus authenticated evidence anchors (turn identifiers and offsets only). Historical failures without versioned evidence remain unknown and are never inferred from duration. The answered_or_voicemail metric deliberately includes only observable SIP/media answer evidence and may include voicemail; human_answered remains not_provable until a separately validated signal exists. Treat pagination as mandatory: a page is not the whole group while pagination.has_more is true.

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: The authenticated organization; must match the bearer workspace.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Project inside the authenticated organization.

parameters.name: external_group_reference
parameters.description: Opaque customer-owned group key. Skysay does not assign campaign, debt, or retry semantics to it.

parameters.name: artifact_readiness
parameters.description: ready requires both an available recording and at least one transcript turn.

parameters.name: platform_exception
parameters.description: Filters only generic platform-quality facts, never customer business classifications.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Opaque page_cursor from the previous response; continue with the returned next_cursor.

200.description: Bounded factual call result page. Server-Timing and X-OpenPhonex-Query-Count describe the fixed read budget; Cache-Control is no-store.

400.description: Missing/malformed group key, filter, limit, or page cursor.

404.description: Project not found in the authenticated organization.

get.summary: Aggregate call volume, talk time, and spend over one or more date windows
get.description: Aggregation runs in SQL over the whole call history for the organization/project, not just a bounded list page, so the figures stay exact however long that history grows. Pass organization_id (and optionally project_id) as query parameters the same way GET /v1/calls does. window is repeated, each in the form <key>:<since-timestamp> (an RFC3339 UTC timestamp); at least one is required and at most 8 may be requested in one call. until is an optional exclusive upper bound (RFC3339 UTC, defaults to now) shared by every window. Pass agent_window naming one of the requested window keys to additionally receive a per-agent breakdown over that one window. That breakdown is a bounded page ordered by agent_id: check agents_has_more and continue with agent_after=<agents_next_cursor> rather than reading one page as the organization's whole agent list. The window totals themselves are never truncated -- they are aggregated in SQL over the entire history in scope.

parameters.name: organization_id
parameters.description: The authenticated organization; must match the bearer's own workspace.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Optional project in the authenticated organization. Omit to aggregate the whole organization.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound shared by every window. Defaults to the current time.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Repeated '<key>:<since>' pairs, e.g. window=today:2026-08-27T00:00:00Z. key is 1-32 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-] and must not repeat across the request. At least one is required.

parameters.name: agent_window
parameters.description: One of the window keys already requested. When set, the response also includes a per-agent breakdown over that window.

parameters.name: agent_limit
parameters.description: Maximum agents in the agent_window breakdown. Validated whenever it is sent -- a non-numeric value is a 400 either way -- but it only changes the response when agent_window is set.

parameters.name: agent_after
parameters.description: Continue the agent breakdown after this agent_id -- pass agents_next_cursor from the previous response. Only changes the response when agent_window is set.

400.description: Missing/duplicate/malformed window, a malformed until, unknown agent_window, or more than 8 windows requested.

get.summary: Get one call
get.description: The same projection GET /v1/calls returns, for a single call. A live browser test (direction=web_test) is a real call and is returned here; a call your agent placed inside a simulation-suite run is platform-synthetic and is not found here.

404.description: Call not found

get.summary: Get one call's full internal lifecycle event log
get.description: One bounded page of this call's call_events rows, oldest first, each with its raw event payload. This is the platform's own internal bookkeeping log, not a webhook replay: it includes types never delivered to any webhook endpoint at all (e.g. wallet.reserved, call.authorization, call.policy_evaluated, number.matched), and every row here is this row's own id/type/payload, never the signed webhook envelope. call.failed is written here too (payload shape varies by writer -- see CallEvent.payload), always thinner than the richer result body its webhook delivers separately. call.completed is the one terminal type NEVER written here at all -- it is derived from the call's final status and delivered only to webhooks; look at status on GET /v1/calls/{call_id} for that outcome instead. The response body is the plain array it has always been; the paging state is in headers. Do NOT read one page as the whole history: check X-Has-More, and continue with after=<the last row's page_cursor> until it is false. A long-running call with many agent tool invocations (each is its own call.agent_tool_call row) is exactly the case that needs more than one page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum events to return in this page.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Continue after a row you already hold: pass its page_cursor. Treat the value as opaque. Unlike an offset it does not move when new events are written mid-walk.

200.description: One page of call events, oldest first

X-Limit.description: The page size actually applied, after clamping.

X-Has-More.description: `true` when older-than-this-page events remain. A page is NOT the whole history unless this is `false`.

X-Next-Cursor.description: Present only when X-Has-More is true: the page_cursor to pass as `after` for the next page.

400.description: limit is not a number or is out of range, or after is not a page cursor.

404.description: Call not found

post.summary: Ask a live call to hang up
post.description: Requests teardown of a call that is already live. Returns 202 with `hangup_requested_at`; it never reports the call as ended, because the media session is torn down by the worker holding it and the call reaches `call.ended` through the ordinary terminal path, recording the reason `hangup_requested`. Repeating the request is idempotent and returns the original timestamp. Until a worker acknowledges, the request stays visible with `status` `pending`. If the worker reports that the teardown FAILED, the call is still up, so a further request re-arms it with a fresh timestamp and the previous failure's reason stays visible beside it; after three consecutive failed teardowns further requests are refused so the call is escalated rather than retried. A call still queued for origination is refused: cancel it with POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/cancel instead. The response carries `hangup_requested_at`, `status` (`pending` or `acknowledged`), `hangup_acknowledged_at`, `hangup_acknowledged_outcome`, `hangup_acknowledged_reason`, `hangup_failed_attempts`, `hangup_unacknowledged_seconds` (null once acknowledged), `hangup_attempt` (which attempt this is; a re-arm increments it) and `already_requested`, which is false for a first or re-armed request and true when an existing one was returned unchanged.

202.description: Hangup requested; not yet acknowledged by the media worker.

409.description: Call is not live: already terminal, or still queued (use cancel).

patch.summary: Choose whether this deployment dials its own outbound calls
patch.description: Sets outbound_execution_mode to 'queue' (the default: admission enqueues a call.outbound_originate job an organization-scoped worker claims) or 'local' (the deployment asks for admission and dials itself, so no organization-scoped credential is needed on that box). Only a self-hosted deployment may be 'local'. The switch is refused in either direction while calls are still in flight -- going local while outbound jobs are still queued would strand them, and going back to queue while the deployment is still dialing locally would abandon those calls. Once the organization has a local-mode deployment and no queue-mode deployment left, a remote POST /v1/calls for its numbers fails closed rather than enqueueing a job nothing would claim.

Gateway tokens require both calls:authorize and gateways:report; missing scopes and a disabled live gate refuse before reservation. Denied authorization returns no token; an idempotency replay returns the original call without a new token. Self-hosted queue-mode workers remain organization-bound. The separately operated platform_hosted mode is internal: it only authorizes an existing hosted call under its current worker lease, deriving tenant/configuration from that call, never creating a caller-selected tenant call. ApiKeyBearer.description: Scoped tai_ bearer keys are required by default for tenant/operator routes. Set OPENPHONEX_AUTH_MODE=development_open only for local demos.

Capabilities.description: The workspace's capabilities record: what it may do outbound. One per workspace, always. `active` authorizes outbound within the listed profiles, channels, destinations and limits; every other status authorizes nothing new.

destination_restrictions.description: Optional customer narrowing, intersected with current capabilities at admission. null means no additional customer restriction.

destination_revision.description: Revision required when saving optional destination restrictions.

all_countries.description: True: every destination except the sanctioned set is authorized and `countries` is empty. False: `countries` is the explicit allowlist. Activation through verification sets it true; a request chooses.

countries.description: The destination allowlist as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes when `all_countries` is false. A call or text to any other country is held for review.

limits.description: The profile caps projected into the workspace's risk controls at its last activation or approval (per-day/per-minute call and SMS counts, unique destinations, daily voice and wallet spend in minor units). Empty when no profile caps were projected. The caps enforced right now are the workspace's risk controls, which an operator may have changed since; `/v1/dashboard/capabilities` reports those.

compliance_profile_id.description: The verified business profile the record was activated against; empty until verification clears.

customer_visible_message.description: Server-composed status sentence for the workspace; display as-is.

approved_by.description: `self_serve` for a request approved within the catalog, the operator who approved it, or the verification door that activated it.

calling_rules.description: The application calling rules an operator recorded on approval; `{}` when none apply.

CapabilitiesProfile.description: One selectable use-case profile and the caps it grants by default.

CapabilitiesUsage.description: Live usage for the same rolling windows the record's limits are expressed in.

CapabilitiesDetail.description: The record, its calling rules, the profiles the workspace may select from, and live usage against its caps.

calling_rules.description: The customer-visible projection of the application calling rules recorded during Skysay approval (effective period, time zone, calling windows, per-case cadence and attempt cap, escalation actions), or null when none apply. Configured by Skysay, never by this API.

calling_rules_active.description: True when calling rules are set and the record is active, i.e. they are enforced on every call right now.

profiles.description: At least one valid use-case profile. Unknown keys are dropped; a selection with none left is refused.

channels.description: Omitted or empty falls back to the selected profiles' own channels.

all_countries.description: True authorizes every destination except the sanctioned set and ignores `countries`. Exactly one of `all_countries: true` or a non-empty `countries` is required; a request with neither is refused with 400 and nothing is written.

countries.description: The destination allowlist as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, used when `all_countries` is not true. An empty list is refused, and so is any entry that is not a well-formed two-letter code once normalized (the refusal names it). A few aliases are normalized (UAE, USA, UK).

limits.description: Optional cap overrides; `live_call_concurrency` is always taken from the plan and never from this payload.

policy_version.description: Accepting the outbound policy here is what makes immediate activation possible for a verified workspace; without it the request goes to review.

metadata.description: Free-form notes merged into the record. `calling_rules` and the retired `metadata.operational_profile` key are refused here: calling rules are set during Skysay approval.

policy_version.description: Required unless the record already carries one.

events.description: Subscribed event types. Omitted or empty at creation defaults to call.created, call.answered, media.started, call.ended, call.completed, call.failed, call.canceled. Change it later with PATCH /v1/agent-endpoints/{agent_endpoint_id}.
The complete replacement subscription list; an empty array is rejected.

VoicePreviewRequest.description: One short synthesis of a bounded caller sentence for a selected TTS voice. Customer requests bind preview spend to the authenticated workspace; organization_id is an optional consistency hint and a foreign value is rejected.

organization_id.description: Optional consistency hint; if supplied, it must match the bearer workspace.

project_id.description: Must belong to the bearer workspace.

voice_id.description: Exact provider voice id. On a platform credential it must be present in the browsable voice inventory, except an existing saved hosted agent may explicitly re-test its exact current selection; with a BYOK credential any id the provider accepts is allowed, so cloned and private voices work.

language.description: Any language the selected provider advertises.

text.description: Optional sentence to speak. Omitted or blank falls back to a short product sample only when no audio_environment is supplied. With an audio_environment it is required and must be non-blank, so the requested text is never silently replaced. It is synthesized, never stored, and never echoed in the response.

audio_environment.description: Optional immutable ambience selection. When present, the preview WAV is a deterministic headroom-safe local audition only; this does not claim a receiver-side final mix. Provider voice and explicit language are unchanged.

delivery.description: Optional delivery profile, the same value an agent stores in `voice_polish.delivery`. The preview applies exactly the provider settings a call with that profile would use; for a provider/model without a truthful control (Fish Audio, Azure) the audio is unchanged and the response reports `delivery_applied: false`.

credential_id.description: Optional selected BYOK credential. It is validated at the provider and then used to render this preview; a platform credential is never a fallback.

agent_id.description: Optional saved hosted agent pin for a managed preview only. It must belong to the authenticated project and exactly match the requested platform-managed provider, model, voice id, and language. It permits re-testing a stored selection missing from the current provider listing; it does not authorize a new voice choice or any BYOK selection.

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides. Each item has locale and optional exact voice, transcriber, and greeting. Omitted values inherit the shared stack; an empty greeting removes its override.

AgentUpdate.description: Mutable agent configuration. The target agent, rather than organization_id or project_id in this body, defines the authenticated workspace boundary. Voice-stack settings are not part of this payload: turn_taking, voice_polish, audio_environment, follow_caller, languages and language_profiles are saved by PATCH /v1/agents/{agent_id}/voice-stack, and sending one here is refused with 400 naming that route rather than accepted and dropped.

oneOf.description: Exact selected TTS provider/model/voice inventory item.

voice_id.description: Provider inventory id, when the selected provider exposes voices.

tools.description: Complete agent tool allowlist. To attach an Integration Action, use an AgentTool object whose type is connection.

project_count.description: Exact number of projects in the bearer organization.

preset_id.description: Exact catalogue id. `off` has no asset.

asset_version.description: Immutable packaged asset version; it is never inferred.

volume.description: Whole-number selection. Off requires 0; enabled presets require 1 through 100.

AudioEnvironmentInvalidSelection.description: A historic malformed saved pin, returned visibly instead of silently becoming Off. Choose a supported selection or Off before publishing again.

CallerInputEnvironmentSelection.description: Simulation Lab only: a version-pinned condition mixed into the synthetic caller microphone. This is not the agent's outgoing audio_environment and never changes a production call's STT/TTS configuration.

preset_id.description: Exact catalogue id. `off` has no asset and is the quiet baseline.

asset_version.description: Immutable packaged asset version; it is never inferred.

noise_level.description: Whole-number caller-input level. Off requires 0; enabled presets require 1 through 100.

AgentTurnTaking.description: Per-agent barge-in and endpointing tuning. Every field is optional and omitted from responses when it is at its default, so an agent that has never configured this section has no `turn_taking` key at all. Applied when a call starts; saving never changes an in-progress call.

interruption_sensitivity.description: Hosted ENGLISH phone calls only; accepted and returned in every language. A preset names an English measurement, so it does not apply to other languages -- set `min_speech_ms`/`silence_hold_ms` explicitly there. Preset interruption threshold: balanced 500 ms, low 750 ms, high 150 ms. `min_speech_ms` takes precedence.

min_speech_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit continuous-speech threshold before an interruption is considered; it overrides any sensitivity preset. On a phone call a value below 500 ms is raised to the 500 ms floor, which exists because shorter bursts of background noise were cutting agents off mid-word. Browser and web calls do not apply this value at all: it is still stored and returned, but those calls keep the stack's own threshold.

silence_hold_ms.description: Hosted phone calls in every language. Explicit endpointing delay after the caller stops speaking; it overrides the platform default hold and any sensitivity preset.

min_interruption_words.description: Defaults to 1 on hosted ENGLISH phone calls and to 0 everywhere else; set 0 explicitly to disable it. When set, an interruption must ALSO carry at least this many recognized words from the caller, in addition to the speech-duration threshold; it never lowers that threshold. On hosted ENGLISH calls, short listening noises ("mm-hm", "uh-huh", "yeah", "okay", "right", "sure", and filler words such as "uh") do not count toward it, so a caller showing they are following does not interrupt; every word counts in other languages. Not English-only, but effective only on stacks whose transcriber reports words fast enough to land inside the decision window (today the Deepgram stacks, English and Estonian). Elsewhere it is stored, returned unchanged, and ignored at call time.

max_call_seconds.description: How long a call may run before the platform ends it and reports `ended_reason: max_call_duration_reached`. Defaults to 1740 (29 minutes), which is also the ceiling: the underlying media session is dropped at 30 minutes, and a limit above that could never fire, so the call would end with no reason attached. Lower it to cap a call sooner; a value outside the range is refused rather than clamped.

no_caller_speech_seconds.description: How long after the call is answered the platform waits to hear the other party before ending the call and reporting `ended_reason: no_caller_speech_after_answer`. Defaults to 20. Speech is detected from the audio itself, not from a transcript, and once the other party has been heard once the rule does not apply again for the rest of that call. The floor is 10 because the witness is voice activity: a caller who is merely listening looks the same as one who is not there, and a shorter value ends the call partway through the agent's own opening line.

barge_in_speech_rms.description: Accepted and returned for compatibility; not applied to call behavior.

AgentVoiceStackUpdate.description: Selection/update payload. It carries only selectors, existing credential IDs, tools, and tuning -- never provider secret material. Supplying languages replaces the selected set; supplying language_profiles replaces sparse overrides, while omission preserves them. After language opt-in, shared prompt, stack, or credential saves explicitly republish inherited effective profiles.

languages.description: When supplied this replaces the selected language set.

language_profiles.description: When supplied this replaces the sparse override set; omit it to preserve overrides.

language_profile_revision.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency revision returned by GET. A stale value returns conflict; reload before retrying.

component_credential_bindings.description: Optional stt/llm/tts map to existing hosted-AI credential IDs (or null to use platform-managed selection). References are validated; secret upload is a separate write-only API.

voice_frontend.description: Optional conversation engine. Omitted or cascade is STT/LLM/TTS. gpt_live selects GPT-Live-1. GET still returns transcriber, model, and voice as an OpenAI compatibility projection.

AgentAcknowledgements.description: Optional short acknowledgement while a slow reply is still being prepared: at most one per caller turn, spoken in the agent's own voice, model and current language on a separate outgoing track, cancelled the moment the real reply starts. Off unless enabled. Without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used; a language without one stays silent rather than switching to English.

phrases.description: Bounded neutral phrases; digits and currency marks are rejected so a phrase cannot carry a factual, payment, legal or consent claim.

delay_ms.description: How long the reply may take before an acknowledgement is worth speaking.

AgentToolWait.description: What the caller hears while a slow tool call (an integration action, a knowledge search) is still running. Off unless a mode is set. `sound` plays a quiet keyboard-typing bed on the separate outgoing track once the tool has run for `delay_ms`, cut the instant the tool finishes, capped at 15 seconds; it is wordless, so it works in every language. `acknowledge` speaks one short phrase in the agent's own voice and language instead; without phrases the platform's reviewed list for the call language is used, and a language without one stays silent. Feedback never plays over the caller or the agent, at most once per tool wait, and never for the built-in end-call or transfer tools.

delay_ms.description: How long a tool may run before feedback starts. Most tools finish well inside this.

phrases.description: For `acknowledge` only; the same bounded neutral-phrase rule as acknowledgements. Rejected with `sound`.

AgentVoicePolish.description: Per-agent voice polish. Absent keys keep the platform defaults; the response omits the section entirely when nothing is configured.

delivery.description: How the selected voice performs its speech. Unset keeps the provider's own defaults, which is what every agent had before this field existed. Each profile maps to allowlisted provider controls only where the selected TTS provider/model truthfully exposes them: ElevenLabs voice settings (eleven_v3 supports stability only), a bounded Gemini TTS synthesis instruction, and a speaking-rate multiplier for Soniox and Cartesia. Fish Audio and Azure neural voices accept the setting but apply no change. The voice preview (POST /v1/voice-previews with the same `delivery`) uses the identical mapping, so an audition sounds like the call.

AgentVoiceStack.description: Safe read projection. It never includes component credential binding IDs, plaintext/ciphertext, nonce, fingerprint, or provider secrets.

voice.description: The stored TTS selection as the agent catalog projects it, including `delivery_control` (`voice_settings`, `instruction`, `speed` or `unsupported`): whether a `voice_polish.delivery` profile changes this voice's audio, and `delivery_profiles`: the exact value each profile resolves to on this engine (empty for `unsupported`), both read from the packaged delivery table.

voice_frontend.description: cascade (default) or gpt_live. Always present on GET; omitted on older rows means cascade.

AgentFollowCaller.description: Explicit saved and published automatic multilingual policy. Existing clients may send only enabled; omitted scope means selected. With scope all, the server resolves every language compatible with the exact stack at publication and freezes that concrete set. With selected, languages supplies the allowed subset. Clients cannot supply runtime adapter options, bindings, or rates.

scope.description: Valid only when enabled. Omit for selected compatibility. All is expanded only at explicit publication and can be unavailable when a provider candidate limit is smaller than the compatible set.

AgentLanguageProfiles.description: Safe editor projection. The immutable runtime profile and credential binding IDs are never returned. Published Follow summaries expose only the frozen allowed locale set, opt-in bit, and opening locale for the authenticated test picker.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 publication time. An empty string with published_version 0 is the legacy-agent sentinel: no language-profile publication exists yet.

published_languages.description: Locales from the immutable published profile set. This is empty when no publication exists.

published_starting_language.description: Frozen Follow opening locale for the published browser-test picker, or an empty string when Follow is not enabled.

workflow.description: Editable draft/revision, validation, and safe canvas-only layout when workflow_state=draft; otherwise null.

layout.description: Only positions, viewport, and collapsed_groups; arbitrary stored layout keys are not returned.

WorkflowVersionSummary.description: Safe immutable version metadata. The separate published field is null before the first explicit publish.

AgentTool.description: A legacy string placeholder, a built-in tool, a signed webhook tool, or an attached Integration Action.

BuiltinAgentTool.description: A built-in tool the AI agent can invoke during a call. `phone_number` is conditionally required: see its own description.

phone_number.description: Destination for `transfer_to_human`, and required when that tool is enabled. Must be full E.164 including the leading `+` and country code (for example `+12025550100`); a blank, partial, or non-dialable number is rejected when the agent is created or updated, rather than failing mid-call. Ignored by `end_call` and `send_sms`.

ended_reason.description: Why the call ended. They fall into three groups. Two are the ordinary end of a call that went well: `agent_completed` when the agent finished the conversation and ended the call itself, which is the usual outcome of a workflow that runs to its last step, and `remote_party_disconnected` when the other party hung up. Three are endings the platform initiates: `hangup_requested` when someone ends the call from the workspace or through POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/hangup, `max_call_duration_reached` when the call hits its configured limit, and `no_caller_speech_after_answer` when the call is answered but nobody ever speaks. The last names an ending nobody chose, neither the people on the call nor the platform: `media_session_lost`, when the media session went away underneath a live call -- the room was deleted, or the connection to it failed -- so nobody hung up, no limit fired and the agent did not finish. It reports what was observed rather than guessing at a cause, so a call that ends this way is not reported as an operator hang-up even when an operator had just asked for one; that request is answered separately and says the call was already gone. Empty on a call that completed before this field shipped, and on a call that has not completed. A call that FAILED reports its reason in `technical_failure.failure_reason_code` instead; the two vocabularies are separate.

type.description: e.g. call.created, call.queued, call.dialing, call.answered, media.started, call.ended, call.failed, call.canceled, call.live_blocked, plus internal-only bookkeeping types such as wallet.reserved, wallet.settled, call.authorization, call.policy_evaluated, number.matched. call.completed is the one terminal type never written here -- it is only ever delivered to webhooks.

payload.description: Event-specific detail; shape varies by writer, not just by type -- call.failed alone has at least four shapes: a policy block carries {reason, reasons}; local/queued-origination failure carries {reason} (the worker-queue originate failure adds worker_job_id and error); a reconciler repair carries {source, reason, previous_status, evidence, observed_at}; a gateway-lifecycle failure (SIP/room) carries an unrelated {gateway_event_id, gateway_id, source_component, source, observed_at, details}. Always thinner than the richer result body the call.failed webhook delivers separately.
